RDHF.settings.pointFormula.name: Feat Points per Character
RDHF.settings.pointFormula.hint: A Roll formula giving a character's lifetime Feat Point total. Use @level, @tier and @prof, or any @system.* path. Default: @level * 2
RDHF.settings.showStatistics.name: Show the Statistics tab
RDHF.settings.showStatistics.hint: Adds a Statistics tab to the Feat Registry, showing how your Feats are distributed across Categories, Levels and Types, and what your table has acquired. Everything it shows is derived on the spot — turning it off stores nothing and loses nothing.
RDHF.settings.menu.name: Feat Registry
RDHF.settings.menu.label: Configure Feats
RDHF.settings.menu.hint: Choose which Features count as Feats, curate their Category, Level, Types and Requirements, and set the Feat Point formula.
RDHF.points.label: Feat Points
RDHF.points.adjustTooltip: GM adjustment to this character's Feat Point total
RDHF.catalog.title: Feats
RDHF.catalog.noAcquired: This character has not acquired any feats yet.
RDHF.catalog.hiddenTooltip: The GM has hidden this feat. Players do not see it in their catalog.
RDHF.catalog.grantedTooltip: Granted by the GM without spending a Feat Point.
RDHF.catalog.investmentsHint: Where you stand in each Category you have Feats in, and what the next Feats in it are waiting on. Reaching a mark clears the investment requirement only — a Feat may still want a Trait, a Level or a prerequisite you do not have yet.
RDHF.catalog.investNone: Nothing left in this Category is waiting on investment.
RDHF.catalog.noInvestments: You have no Feats yet, so there is nothing invested to report. Take one from the Catalog and this tab will track where it leads.
RDHF.catalog.newTooltip: One of the ten most recently curated Feats.
RDHF.catalog.uncuratedTooltip: No Category set — players cannot see this feat yet.
RDHF.catalog.acquireTooltip: Spend a Feat Point on this feat
RDHF.catalog.noFeats: No feats are available yet. A GM sets them up in the Feat Registry.
RDHF.dialog.acquireWarning: This cannot be reversed without GM intervention.
RDHF.dialog.reasonOwned: You have already acquired this feat.
RDHF.dialog.reasonNoPoints: You have no Feat Points left to spend.
RDHF.dialog.grantBody: Grant this feat regardless of its requirements?
RDHF.dialog.grantCharge: Charge a Feat Point for it
RDHF.dialog.revokeBody: Remove {name} from this character and refund its Feat Point? The granted Feature item will be deleted.
RDHF.registry.title: Feat Registry
RDHF.registry.sourcesHint: Register a compendium and every Feature inside it becomes a Feat. Feats stay hidden from players until you give them a Category.
RDHF.registry.dropHint: …or drag a single Feature item anywhere onto this window to register just that one.
RDHF.registry.standaloneHint: Features you dragged in one at a time, rather than through a compendium source.
RDHF.registry.noStandalone: None yet — drag a Feature item onto this window to add one.
RDHF.registry.unregisterBody: Unregister {name}? It was added on its own rather than through a source pack, so this removes it from the module entirely along with all of its curation. Characters who already acquired it keep their copy.
RDHF.registry.resetFeatBody: Clear the Category, Types, summary and every requirement on {name}? It stays registered and returns to uncurated, so players will not see it until you file it again.
RDHF.curation.queueEmpty: Nothing is waiting to be curated.
RDHF.curation.doneHint: Every registered Feat has a Category, so players can see all of them. Register another source, or refine what you have on the Feats tab.
RDHF.curation.fileTooltip: Save this Feat to the world and move on. Only this Feat is written — sources, taxonomy and the point formula still need Save.
RDHF.curation.fileUncuratedNote: This Feat has no Category yet. Filing it moves you on, but it is still hidden from players and will be back in the queue next time you open the Registry.
RDHF.notify.fileFailed: Could not save that Feat. Nothing was written.
RDHF.registry.unsavedBody: The Feat Registry has changes that have not been saved. Closing now discards them.
RDHF.registry.standaloneTooltip: Registered individually by drag and drop, not from a compendium source.
RDHF.registry.resyncAllTooltip: Rewrite every owned copy of every registered Feat from its source item.
RDHF.registry.resyncFeatTooltip: Re-sync this Feat on every character who owns it.
RDHF.registry.resyncFeatBody: Rewrite {name} on {count} character copy/copies from its source item?
RDHF.registry.resyncAllBody: Rewrite {count} owned copies of {feats} Feat(s) across {characters} character(s) from their source items?
RDHF.registry.resyncWarning: Name, image, description, actions and effects are replaced. Any edits made to a character’s own copy are lost.
RDHF.registry.noFeats: Nothing to curate. Register a compendium or drop a Feature in the Sources tab.
RDHF.registry.noMatches: No registered feats match this search.
RDHF.registry.autoExemptHint: This Feat is left exactly as authored, whatever the Automation tab has switched on. Use it for the exceptions a rule should not reach.
RDHF.registry.autoInvestment: Automation adds this: {count} Feats already acquired in {category}, from this Feat's Level {level}. Add a row below to replace it.
RDHF.registry.autoInvestmentPending: Automation is on: once this Feat has a Category other than General, it will ask for {count} Feats already acquired in that Category, from its Level {level}. Add a row below to replace it.
RDHF.registry.autoInvestmentOverridden: Your row below replaces the automatic requirement, which would have asked for {count} in {category}.
RDHF.registry.autoInvestmentExempt: This Feat ignores Rule Automation. Without that tick it would ask for {count} in its own Category.
RDHF.registry.autoInvestmentGeneral: Automation never adds a requirement to a General Feat, so this one is unaffected.
RDHF.registry.hiddenHint: A hidden feat is never listed in the player catalog, even once it has a Category. A character who has already acquired it keeps seeing it under My Feats.
RDHF.registry.summaryHint: Shown on the collapsed catalog row. Leave blank to use the start of the feat's own description.
RDHF.registry.investmentHint: Rows are read left to right, AND before OR — "Alchemy ×2 AND Arcana ×1 OR Swordmaster ×3" means either both of the first two, or the last one on its own.
RDHF.registry.fixedCategoryTooltip: General is a fixed Category. It cannot be renamed or deleted, so a feat can always be curated without inventing a filing system.
RDHF.registry.resourcesHint: Compared against the character's maximum, not their current value.
RDHF.registry.featuresPlaceholder: Comma-separated Feature names or feat UUIDs (any one satisfies)
RDHF.registry.featuresDropHint: Search by name, or drag a Feat or Feature straight onto this block. Any one of these satisfies the requirement.
RDHF.registry.expressionHint: Optional. Combine atoms with AND / OR — for example: classIs:Rogue AND tierAtLeast:2
RDHF.registry.atomTooltip: Append this condition to the expression
RDHF.registry.categoriesHint: A Feat belongs to exactly one Category. Categories drive the catalog filters and Investment requirements. Hide one to withhold every Feat filed under it.
RDHF.registry.typesHint: Types are free-form tags. Add Class or Domain names here to tag feats with them. Hide one to withhold every Feat carrying it, even if its other Types are visible.
RDHF.registry.withheldByCategory: This Category is hidden, so players do not see this Feat. Untick it on the Taxonomy tab to restore it.
RDHF.registry.withheldByType: This Type is hidden, so players do not see this Feat even if its other Types are visible. Untick it on the Taxonomy tab to restore it.
RDHF.registry.taxonomyHiddenHint: Hidden from players. Feats are withheld from the catalog and this entry is dropped from the filter rail. You still see and file into it, and a character keeps any Feat they already own.
RDHF.registry.deleteCategoryInUse: {count} feat(s) use this category. Deleting it makes them uncurated and hides them from players until you re-file them. Continue?
RDHF.registry.deleteTypeBody: Delete this type? It will be removed from every feat that carries it.
RDHF.registry.formulaPreview: At level 1 this grants {value} Feat Point(s).
RDHF.registry.formulaInvalid: This formula does not evaluate — check the @keys.
RDHF.registry.importBody: This replaces the entire registry, taxonomy and point formula in this editor. Nothing is written until you press Save.
RDHF.notify.noPermission: You do not have permission to view this character's feats.
RDHF.notify.notAFeature: Only Feature items can be registered as Feats.
RDHF.notify.dropOnZone: Drop a Feature on the drop zone in the Sources tab to register it as a Feat.
RDHF.notify.resyncNobody: No character owns a copy to re-sync.
RDHF.notify.resyncMissing: {count} registered Feat(s) could not be resolved and were skipped.
RDHF.notify.fixedCategory: The General Category cannot be deleted.
RDHF.notify.migrationFailed: Hero Feats could not migrate this world’s data. See the console; it will try again on the next load.
RDHF.notify.migratedGeneral: Hero Feats: General is now a Category. {filed} feat(s) filed under it, {stripped} updated.
RDHF.notify.sourceMissing: The source item for this feat could not be found ({uuid}).
RDHF.notify.grantFailed: The feat could not be added to this character.
RDHF.notify.importInvalid: That file is not a valid Feat Registry export.
RDHF.automation.intro: Rules that derive requirements for every Feat at once, instead of you typing the same requirement onto each of them. Nothing is written into your Feats — switching a rule off restores the catalog exactly as you authored it.
RDHF.automation.investment.name: Default Investment by Level
RDHF.automation.investment.toggle: Require investment in a Feat's own Category, by its Level
RDHF.automation.investment.hint: While this is on, a Feat asks the character to already own a number of Feats in that same Category, taken from the table below. It counts acquired Feats, GM grants included, at any Level.
RDHF.automation.exempt.general: The General Category is never affected — it is the Category a Feat can be filed under before you have invented a filing system, so gating its own entry point would make it unusable.
RDHF.automation.exempt.uncurated: Uncurated Feats are never affected: with no Category there is nothing to require investment in.
RDHF.automation.exempt.authored: A Feat that already carries its own Investment in Category rows keeps them, and the rule stands aside. The exception is a single row that states exactly what the rule would — that Feat is adopted by the rule and the now-redundant row is cleared on Save, so it follows the table if you retune it later.
RDHF.automation.exempt.flag: Any single Feat can opt out with "Ignore Rule Automation" on the Feats or Curation tab.
RDHF.automation.tableHint: Feats already acquired in the Category, required before a Feat of that Level in it becomes available. A Level above the table uses the highest row; 0 means no requirement.
RDHF.stats.gridHint: Feats per Level. Shading is relative to the busiest cell in this grid — click any cell to open the Feats tab filtered to it.
RDHF.stats.typedNote: Feats carrying at least one Type:
RDHF.stats.emptyLevels: Levels with no Feats at any Category:
RDHF.stats.emptyCells: Category and Level combinations with nothing in them:
RDHF.stats.noGaps: Every Category has a Feat at every Level.
RDHF.stats.reachHint: Every Investment in Category requirement, whether you wrote it or the Automation curve derived it. A Feat is reachable only when enough Feats in the Category it asks for, at or below its own Level, are themselves reachable — so a row of Feats that only supply each other counts for nothing, and Feats withheld from players count for nothing either. Trait minimums and prerequisites on those supplying Feats are still not modelled, so passing means "not provably impossible", not "comfortable".
RDHF.stats.reachNone: No Feat carries an Investment in Category requirement, authored or derived, so there is nothing that could be unreachable.
RDHF.stats.reachClean: Every Feat that asks for investment can be reached. Checked:
RDHF.stats.reachBlocked: Feats that can never be acquired:
RDHF.stats.brokenRefsHint: These Feats require another Feat by UUID that is no longer registered. A requirement naming a Feature by plain text is never listed here — it is matched loosely by design.
RDHF.stats.requirementUsageHint: Counts the requirements you authored on each Feat.
RDHF.stats.requirementUsageAutoHint: Rule Automation is on, so most Feats also carry a derived Investment in Category requirement. Those are not counted here — the rule reaches nearly every Feat, and including them would peg that bar at 100% and tell you nothing. What the rule demands of your catalog is reported under Unreachable Feats, above.
RDHF.stats.traitDemandHint: How many Feats gate on each Trait. A catalog that leans hard on one Trait leaves characters built any other way with little to buy.
RDHF.stats.ledgerExcludeHint: Set a character aside to leave them out of the figures below — a retired hero, an NPC sheet, a test dummy. They stay in the table so you can bring them back, and nothing about their own Feats changes.
RDHF.stats.ledgerHint: Only characters who own at least one Feat are listed.
RDHF.stats.noFeats: No Feats registered yet. Add a source or drop a Feature on the Sources tab, and this tab will show how your catalog is shaped.
RDHF.stats.noPlayData: No character owns a Feat yet. This section fills in as your table starts spending Feat Points.
